summary: Assemble and adversarially review one paper from an existing parseable A11 recipe, stopping at the human-signature gate.
applies_when: Conservative router: choose this only when the origin issue text unambiguously matches this flow and exactly one flow. It must request pre-sign production for ONE paper, name one EXISTING `Papers/recipes/<THEORY-Pnnn>.yaml` A11 recipe, state that the recipe is fully parseable, and state that an executable deterministic `Meta/papergen` already exists. It must request BOTH deterministic assembly and claim-by-claim adversary review. Positive fixture: assemble and adversarially review `Papers/recipes/D5-P001.yaml` with the existing papergen, stopping before signature. Near-miss fixtures that MUST choose none/plain devloop: implement papergen; create or repair a recipe; request a paper without one exact recipe; sign, freeze, tag, assign a DOI, publish, or add errata; run a recurring all-recipes cron; or any ambiguous/broad request. This workflow ends at `adversary-reviewed`; when in doubt choose none/plain devloop.

steps.title: Assemble and adversarially review the pre-sign paper package

content.generator:
Read the origin issue through its source_ref and emit exactly one child issue title and body for the combined papergen-assemble-and-adversary-review step. Scope the child to ONE named paper recipe and perform deterministic pre-sign assembly followed immediately by claim-by-claim adversary review in the same execution workspace. All governing rules are embedded below; do NOT consult an external specification.

PRECONDITION (FAIL CLOSED): the origin must name exactly one existing `Papers/recipes/<paper-id>.yaml`; `<paper-id>` must be an A11 id of the form `<THEORY>-P<three digits>`; the recipe must parse with exactly `{id, decls, blueprint, evidence, narrative_order, venue}`; `id` must equal the path id; `decls`, `blueprint`, and `evidence` must contain canonical full GIDs; and an executable deterministic `Meta/papergen` must already exist. Full GID grammar is `THEORY/[PLANE/]PATH[.DECL][--TAG]`. Formal declaration GIDs omit the F plane and include `.DECL`, for example `D5/S3/Diffraction/Avoidance.peak_height`; Blueprint GIDs include `/B/`, for example `D5/B/S3/Diffraction/Avoidance`; Evidence GIDs include `/E/`, a declaration selector, and an artifact tag, for example `D5/E/S3/Diffraction/Avoidance.zeros_scan--json`. Resolve every referenced GID and reject missing, ambiguous, wildcard, shorthand, or non-canonical references. Do not create or repair a recipe and do not implement, scaffold, or modify papergen merely to satisfy this precondition. If any precondition is absent or false, require NO changes and a precise WHY; no-changes is fatal and blocks the origin.

ASSEMBLY: invoke the existing papergen for that recipe. It must deterministically read canonical typed Blueprint narrative, Library citations, and Evidence figures, then emit LaTeX and one arXiv-ready package. A clean rerun from the same repository tree and recipe bytes must produce byte-identical output. Generated build output is a projection and must not be committed.

STATUS BADGES ARE SYNTAX, NEVER PROSE: derive every rendered mathematical-status badge from the referenced Lean declaration and its axiom closure. PROVED means no `sorry` and closure contained in `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`. AXIOM-CARRYING means the closure includes an axiom registered in `AxiomDebt.lean`. CONDITIONAL means the declaration signature carries `(h : Assumptions.X)`. OPEN means a declaration under `X_Frontier/` carries `sorry`; `sorry` anywhere else is an error. Never promote OPEN, CONDITIONAL, or AXIOM-CARRYING text to a theorem badge.

MACHINE ASSEMBLY RECEIPT: require papergen to place canonical JSON `assembly-receipt.json` inside the generated package with schema `fkst.paper-assembly.v1` and fields `{paper_id, recipe_sha256, source_tree_oid, payload, package_sha256, claims}`. `source_tree_oid` is the exact Git tree object id used for assembly. `payload` lists every generated non-receipt file exactly once as `{path, sha256}`, sorted by ASCII path; `package_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of that payload array, so adding either receipt cannot change it. `claims` is in narrative order and contains exactly one entry per rendered claim: `{claim_id, source_gid, code_status, rendered_badge}`. GIDs must resolve and claim ids must be unique. Validate the receipt with the existing papergen before review.

SAME-EXECUTION HANDOFF: keep the generated package and validated `assembly-receipt.json` in the same execution workspace through adversary review. Review those exact package bytes; do not fetch a predecessor result, rebuild from a later repository state, or substitute another package. Resolve and recompute every source claim from the exact Git tree identified by `source_tree_oid`, not from a mutable current checkout. A missing tree object, package file, receipt, or hash match is a blocking review failure.

CLAIM-BY-CLAIM ADVERSARY REVIEW: for every assembly claim, recompute its syntax-derived code status and allowed badge from `source_tree_oid` and compare both with the rendered paper. Challenge theorem strength, assumptions, axiom closure, `sorry`, citation support, and Evidence provenance. Review every claim exactly once; a prose-only approval is forbidden. OPEN, CONDITIONAL, and AXIOM-CARRYING claims must remain visibly distinguished from PROVED claims. Any unsupported strengthening or stale status is a failed claim and blocks completion. Do not edit the recipe, papergen, source claims, or generated prose merely to make review pass.

MACHINE REVIEW RECEIPT: emit canonical JSON `adversary-review-receipt.json` inside the same pre-sign package with schema `fkst.paper-adversary-review.v1` and fields `{paper_id, recipe_sha256, source_tree_oid, package_sha256, claims, verdict}`. Preserve assembly claim order. Each review entry is exactly `{claim_id, source_gid, code_status, rendered_badge, verdict, finding}` with `verdict` in `{pass, fail}` and a non-empty finding. `verdict` is `pass` only when all hashes and the source tree object id match, every assembly claim appears exactly once, every claim verdict is `pass`, and no extra claim exists. Validate the receipt by machine; do not accept a hand-written summary as the receipt.

TERMINAL BOUNDARY: successful completion records only `adversary-reviewed` and prepares the package for the separate human-signature gate. `human-signed`, `frozen`, content hash/tag/DOI release, publication, and post-publication errata are outside this workflow and MUST NOT be performed or claimed. Generated build/review output is not committed. The child PR may contain only source/test changes genuinely necessary for the combined bounded step, and TDD/tests live inside this child PR. Do not ask the child to duplicate devloop consensus, CI, PR review, or merge gates; devloop provides those. If no independently mergeable source/test increment exists, require NO changes with a clear WHY; no-changes is fatal and blocks the origin.
